bug_info.bug_desc: In the pre-merge code, the command/address FIFO write enable was generated by a standalone continuous assignment: sck_cmdaddr_wvalid = (cmdaddr_bitcnt == 5'h1F) && !is_hw_reg. This condition only excluded hardware-handled registers and did not also exclude invalid-locality reads. Because is_hw_reg is itself gated by !invalid_locality, a read to an unsupported locality with cfg_tpm_invalid_locality_i enabled still pushed a command/address entry into the CmdAddr FIFO, even though the TPM returns 0xFF directly from hardware and the spec says invalid-locality reads must not enqueue the command and address. This causes software to see and process stale/spurious CMDADDR entries, and can overflow or drop later valid commands if software does not clear the FIFO promptly.
bug_info.fix_hint: Make the CmdAddr FIFO push enable a per-transaction control decision rather than a global !is_hw_reg expression. Default sck_cmdaddr_wvalid to 0 in the FSM combinational block, and assert it only in the StAddr end-of-address branches that actually forward the transaction to software: software-handled reads (non-TPM-register/CRB-mode reads and the fallback software-read case) and all writes. Keep it deasserted for hardware-handled reads and for invalid-locality reads that return INVALID bytes, so those accesses are not enqueued.
